title: Every reference to every Objective-C ivar offset cell in the pinned ELF
mechanism: ivar offset cell reached via a .got entry whose file contents are the cell VA
method: OBJC_IVAR_$_C.i denotes a 4-byte cell in __objc_ivar; code reaches it through a two-word PIC idiom whose middle address is a .got entry, and *that entry's file contents are the cell VA*. A reference exists exactly when *(wA + v) is a known cell VA, v being the PIC base 0x105faf4.

World.worldTime.conclusion: three references, ALL reads - so the 20-units-per-second clock is not advanced by any ivar store in this library

World.fastForward.conclusion: exactly one reference, the byte read in its own getter - no writer at all in this library, and no overlapping neighbour (934 is a standalone char between 933 idleTimerDisabled and 936 saveCount)

literal_offset_half.what: the complement sweep: stores with a literal offset #0x288 (648) / #0x3a6 (934) anywhere in the code window
literal_offset_half.result: no World-object field store: the hits are stack slots ([sp, #0x648] / [sp, #0x3a4]) or draw-buffer offsets - dozens of -draw: methods write a vertex buffer at 0x648, which is why a naive literal sweep looks alarming
literal_offset_half.conclusion: neither field is written by a cell-based OR a literal-offset store

boundary: The access classification is heuristic: it reads the instruction sequence after the site. It was hand-verified against four known sites (the worldTime getter, two worldTime reads, the fastForward getter) and four earlier classification bugs were found by the self-check.
Absence of a write is a statement about THIS library. A bulk memcpy into the object, an object built from serialized data, or another library in the APK are all still open.

Method attribution is reported with its basis: unique / ambiguous / none, plus every method-table entry in [fn_start, site]. The fastForward site is 'ambiguous' on purpose - it sits in a run of one-line getters (startPortalPos, serverClients, server, client, fastForward, doubleTimeUnlocked) sharing one body.
